readings.title: The Sons of Keturah
readings.text: [Genesis 25:1] And Abraham took another wife, and her name was Qeturah. [2] And she bore him <dn>את</dn> Zimran, and <dn>את</dn> Yoqshan, and <dn>את</dn> Medan, and <dn>את</dn> Miḏyan, and <dn>את</dn> Yishbaq, and <dn>את</dn> Shuaḥ. [3] And Yoqshan brought forth <dn>את</dn> Sheḇa and <dn>את</dn> Dedan. And the sons of Dedan were Asshurim, and Letushim, and Le’ummim. [4] And the sons of Miḏyan: Ephah, and Ep̄er, and Ḥanoḵ, and Aḇiḏa, and Elda’ah. All these were the children of Qeturah.

readings.title: The Chronicles Record of Keturah
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 1:32] And the sons of Qeturah, Abraham’s concubine: she bore <dn>את</dn> Zimran, and <dn>את</dn> Yoqshan, and <dn>את</dn> Medan, and <dn>את</dn> Miḏyan, and <dn>את</dn> Yishbaq, and <dn>את</dn> Shuaḥ. And the sons of Yoqshan: Sheḇa and Dedan. [33] And the sons of Miḏyan: Ephah, and Ep̄er, and Ḥanoḵ, and Aḇiḏa, and Elda’ah. All these were the sons of Qeturah.

readings.title: Inheritance and Separation
readings.text: [Genesis 25:5] And Abraham gave <dn>את</dn> all that he had to Yitsḥaq. [6] But to the sons of the concubines whom Abraham had, Abraham gave gifts, and while he was still living he sent them eastward, away from Yitsḥaq his son, to the land of the east.

readings.title: The Generations of Ishmael
readings.text: [Genesis 25:12] And this is the genealogy of Yishmaʽĕl, Abraham’s son, whom Hag̱ar the Mitsrite, Sarah’s female servant, bore to Abraham. [13] And these were the names of the sons of Yishmaʽĕl, by their names, according to their generations: The first-born of Yishmaʽĕl, Neḇayoth; then Qĕḏar, and Aḏbe’ĕl, and Miḇsam, [14] and Mishma, and Dumah, and Massa, [15] Ḥaḏad, and Tĕma, Yetur, Naphish, and Qeḏmah. [16] These were the sons of Yishmaʽĕl and these were their names, by their towns and their settlements, twelve princes according to their nations. [17] And these were the years of the life of Yishmaʽĕl: one hundred and thirty-seven years. And he breathed his last and died, and was gathered to his people. [18] And they dwelt from Ḥawilah as far as Shur, which is east of Mitsrayim as you go toward Ashshur. He settled before all his brothers.

readings.title: The Chronicles Record of Ishmael
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 1:28] The sons of Abraham: Yitsḥaq and Yishmaʽĕl. [29] These are their genealogies: The first-born of Yishmaʽĕl was Neḇayoth; then Qĕḏar, and Aḏbe’ĕl, and Miḇsam, [30] Mishma, and Dumah, Massa, Ḥaḏad, and Tĕma, [31] Yetur, Naphish, and Qeḏmah. These were the sons of Yishmaʽĕl.

readings.title: The Chronicles Record of Isaac
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 1:34] And Abraham brought forth <dn>את</dn> Yitsḥaq. The sons of Yitsḥaq: Ěsaw and Yisra’ĕl.

readings.title: The Birth of Esau and Jacob
readings.text: [Genesis 25:19] And this is the genealogy of Yitsḥaq, Abraham’s son. Abraham brought forth <dn>את</dn> Yitsḥaq. [20] And Yitsḥaq was forty years old when he took <dn>את</dn> Riḇqah as wife, the daughter of Bethu’ĕl the Aramean of Paddan Aram, the sister of Laḇan the Aramean. [21] And Yitsḥaq prayed to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for his wife, because she was barren. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> answered his prayer, and Riḇqah his wife conceived. [22] And the children struggled together within her; and she said, “If it is so, why am I thus?” So she went to inquire of <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [23] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to her, <dq>“Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples shall be separated from your body. And one people shall be stronger than the other, and the older serve the younger.”</dq> [24] And when the days were filled for her to give birth, see, there were twins in her womb. [25] And the first came out red all over, like a hairy garment, so they called his name Ěsaw. [26] And afterward his brother came out, and his hand took hold of Ěsaw’s heel, so his name was called Yaʽaqoḇ. And Yitsḥaq was sixty years old when she bore <dn>את</dn> them.

readings.title: The Death of Abraham
readings.text: [Genesis 25:7] And these are the days of the years of the life of Abraham which he lived: one hundred and seventy-five years. [8] And Abraham breathed his last and died in a good old age, an old man and satisfied, and was gathered to his people. [9] And his sons Yitsḥaq and Yishmaʽĕl buried <dn>את</dn> him in the cave of Maḵpelah, which is before Mamrĕ, in the field of Ephron son of Tsoḥar the Ḥittite, [10] the field which Abraham purchased from the sons of Ḥeth. There Abraham was buried, and Sarah his wife. [11] And it came to be, after the death of Abraham, that <dn>Elohim</dn> blessed <dn>את</dn> his son Yitsḥaq. And Yitsḥaq dwelt at Be’ĕr Laḥai Ro’i.
